portfolio:brief.summary: You've finished a heavy de-risking pass — six positions closed this week, the semi trading names are out, and the book that's left is a clean AI-infrastructure core that needs patience, not more surgery.
insights: The repositioning is done: AMZN, TSM, MU, AMD, TEM, PATH, NTAP and NEE are all closed, and what remains is 15 quality names rather than a scattered list of trades.
Overall the book is down just 1.5% since inception with a 25% swing rate — that's a normal aggressive-growth ride, not a problem, and the worst drawdown you've sat through was 14.5%.

Today's -1.13% is concentrated in three names — VRT down 8.1% into earnings tomorrow, GEV down 6.1%, ETN down 3.6% — while GOOGL, MSFT, LLY and CRWD all rose, which is exactly how a mixed book is supposed to behave.
Your winners are the quiet ones: AAPL up 10.4% and NET up 9.1% are carrying the book while the newer AI-infrastructure adds sit slightly underwater and haven't had time to work yet.
Cash is $210, about 2% of the account — small, but this is risk capital and it's better used on one real buy than spread thin across four.
mix: AI Infrastructure at 32% plus AI at 22% means over half the book rides the same datacenter build-out — that is your conviction bet and it is intentional, but it's the one number to watch.
Compute Power 16% and Energy 14% add up to 30% in the power-for-AI trade, which is genuinely a second bet on the same theme rather than a diversifier.
Healthcare 7% (LLY) and Tech 7% (AAPL) are your only true offsets and both are working — these are the parts of the book you should be growing, not trimming.
No formal targets exist for this account, so the honest read is: concentration is high by design and appropriate for an aggressive mandate, but a new dollar belongs outside AI infrastructure.
positions: NVDA is your anchor at 16.6% of the book and down 2.7% — it has gone sideways for weeks while the business keeps compounding, and that patience is the position.
AAPL is your best holding at +10.4% with earnings in two days and sitting near its 52-week high — hold it, don't take a short-term gain right before the print.
VRT fell 8.1% today with earnings tomorrow, and it's your third-largest position at $1,057 — expect a sharp move either way and do not touch it before the number.
GEV is your smallest position at $153 and down 7.6% after a 6.1% drop today — it is too small to hurt you, so let it be rather than trading a $153 stub.
actions: Buy $200 of LLY near $660 level on any dip.
Do not trade VRT or MSFT before earnings tomorrow.
risks: Over half the book rides the AI datacenter build-out; a weak VRT or MSFT print tomorrow would hit NVDA, AVGO, VRT, CEG and ETN together.
VRT closing below roughly $88 after earnings would confirm the power-and-cooling trade is losing its bid, not just wobbling.
scout: HIGH CONVICTION UNH — the largest US health insurer trading at a fraction of its historic multiple after a brutal reset; start $200 on any weakness, target a 50% recovery over two years.
HIGH CONVICTION V — a toll booth on every card swipe with 60%+ margins and no AI exposure at all; buy $200 on a pullback, compounds low-teens for years.
SPECULATIVE UPSIDE OKLO — small modular nuclear aimed directly at datacenter power demand, pre-revenue and volatile; risk only $100 you can lose entirely, multi-bagger if a reactor gets approved.
HIGH CONVICTION COST — membership fees that renew at 90%+ and pricing power in any economy; a boring anchor to own for a decade, buy $150 on a dip.
